Day One
I’ve sailed for many years, but never have I faced such a storm surge.
The waves threw me onto the beach like flotsam—what a disgrace to an old sailor like me.
Fortunately, there is enough wild fruit and fresh water near the beach so I don’t need to worry about starving.
I’ll just wait for the storm to die down and then set sail again.

Day Four
I built a shelter to keep me out of the rain—it looks sturdy enough.
I was shocked to see an Echoback stranded on the beach.
It looks young—perhaps the storm messed with its echolocation.
I’ll try to take it back home once the storm stops.

Day Seven
Another shelter destroyed by the storm... That makes three now. The storm shows no sign of stopping.
More and more Echobacks are getting stranded. It’s strange since they almost never get lost at sea.
I can’t even remember how many times their singing has guided me out of storms.
Now we’re trapped on this beach together, and there’s nothing I can do to help them but listen to their wailing all day long in the pouring rain.
I pray to you, Aeolus.
Please help us through the storm and guide us home safely.

Day Ten
I’ve lost another shelter. I’m too tired to build more.
Almighty Aeolus, am I going to die in this foreign land’s endless storm?

Day Eleven
This has to be the most unbelievable scene I’ve witnessed in my entire life.
An enormous Echoback showed up in the storm and guided his struggling brothers and sisters back into the depths of the sea, one by one.
His powerful singing even drowned out the howling winds and thunder. He just kept singing until all the stranded Echobacks found their way back.
Watching his figure swimming through the waves, I realized that no storm lasts forever. 
Just like every storm I’ve been through, they always end with blue skies.

Day Fifteen
The storm has finally stopped.
I didn’t fail my reputation as an old sailor, just like the Echoback didn’t fail his brothers and sisters.
He brought them all back to the sea, but stayed behind... forever, on this shore.
The raft I made was too small to tow him, so I could only carve my journal into this stone.
I know that his bones will stand here for a very long time.

May his life outlast even this story.
May all sailors finally see their blue skies.
